title: 7D quiz (25 marks) and mark scheme
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Ecosystems (7D); atoms, elements and molecules (7H)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 57 (7D quiz (25 marks) and mark scheme (portal))
intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: Blood group is an example of...
questions.a: B) Discontinuous, inherited. Blood group has fixed groups (A, B, AB, O) and comes from parents.

questions.q: Small ears on an Arctic fox help it...
questions.a: B) Lose less heat. Smaller surface area means less heat lost.

questions.q: A hedgehog sleeps through winter. This is...
questions.a: B) Hibernation. Hibernation saves energy when food is scarce.

questions.q: Two plant species grow close together. They compete for...
questions.a: A) Light and water. Plants need light and water; territory and mates are animal resources.

questions.q: Grey squirrels harm red squirrels mainly by...
options: Competing for food and spreading disease
questions.a: B) Competing for food and spreading disease. They out-compete reds and carry squirrelpox.

questions.q: In 'grass → rabbit → fox', the fox is the...
questions.a: C) Secondary consumer. The fox eats the primary consumer (rabbit).

questions.q: Sort 12 features on the sheet into continuous or discontinuous, and inherited, environmental or both.
questions.a: Correct sort as on the answer sheet (e.g. height: continuous, both; blood group: discontinuous, inherited)
questions.model: Teacher sorts 'height' first: 'any value, so continuous; genes and diet, so both'.

questions.q: Measure the hand span of everyone at home and group the results into classes.
questions.a: A tally table with 1 cm classes

questions.q: Why do identical twins still show some differences?
questions.a: They share genes, so differences must come from the environment

questions.q: Is mass continuous or discontinuous? Inherited, environmental or both?
questions.model: Can mass be any value in a range? Yes: continuous. Do genes affect it? Yes. Does diet? Yes. So both.

questions.q: Which graph for shoe sizes in a class?
Choose a camel, a fish or a water lily. Draw it and label four adaptations with how each helps.
questions.a: Four correct adaptations with reasons, e.g. camel: hump of fat, wide feet, long eyelashes, can go days without drinking
questions.model: Teacher labels the camel's long eyelashes: 'keep sand out of the eyes in sandstorms'.

questions.q: Design a plant for a dark rainforest floor. Give three adaptations.
questions.a: e.g. large leaves to catch dim light, drip tips, shallow roots

questions.q: Why might an animal well adapted to one place struggle if the climate changes?
questions.a: Its features suit the old conditions; it may not survive the new ones

questions.q: A fennec fox lives in a hot desert and has huge ears. Explain why.
questions.a: Large ears give a big surface area to lose heat (and to hear prey)
questions.model: Compare with the Arctic fox: small ears keep heat in. The desert is hot, so the fox needs to lose heat. Large ears lose more heat.
